Class AbstractGTNetMessageHandler

java.lang.Object
grafiosch.gtnet.handler.AbstractGTNetMessageHandler
All Implemented Interfaces:
GTNetMessageHandler
Direct Known Subclasses:
AbstractAnnouncementHandler, AbstractRequestHandler, AbstractResponseHandler, ExchangeSyncHandler, HistoryquoteCoverageHandler, HistoryquoteExchangeHandler, HistoryquotePushHandler, LastpriceExchangeHandler, LastpricePushHandler, PingMessageHandler, SecurityBatchLookupHandler, SecurityLookupHandler
public abstract class AbstractGTNetMessageHandler extends Object implements GTNetMessageHandler
Abstract base class providing common functionality for GTNet message handlers. Provides utility methods for:
  • Storing incoming messages
  • Building response envelopes
  • Converting between POJOs and parameter maps
Subclasses should typically extend the more specialized AbstractRequestHandler or AbstractAnnouncementHandler instead of this class directly.

  • Method Details

    • storeIncomingMessage

      protected GTNetMessage storeIncomingMessage(GTNetMessageContext context)
      Stores the incoming message in the database, or returns the row a previous delivery of the same message already created.

      A redelivery is a normal event rather than an edge case: both delivery tasks re-send the same persisted GTNetMessage and the envelope carries its id unchanged, so a retry after a lost response is byte-identical. uk_gt_net_message_source makes a second insert a constraint violation, so the lookup comes first. Most duplicates never reach a handler at all — they are answered from the stored outcome before dispatch — but a query handler that is safe to re-run does reach this point, and must not insert again.

      A message that names a local one as what it answers is threaded under it. That is what makes the visibility of the conversation apply to it: an inbound admin message used to be stored with replyTo == null whatever the peer said it was answering, so a reply into an ADMIN_ONLY thread was stored with whatever visibility byte the peer had chosen. The id is not taken on trust — the envelope validator has already resolved it against a local message of this same peer, so it cannot thread under another peer's conversation.

      Parameters:
      context - the message context
      Returns:
      the persisted GTNetMessage entity, existing or new

    • triggerExchangeSyncTask

      protected void triggerExchangeSyncTask(GTNetMessageContext context)
      Schedules the exchange configuration synchronisation after a data exchange has been agreed.

      Called from both sides of the negotiation, so a freshly accepted pair holds its supplier-detail rows without waiting for the next daily run. Does nothing when the application publishes no IExchangeSyncTrigger, which is the case for the library stack.

      Parameters:
      context - the message context of the accepted exchange

    • recordLimitViolation

      protected void recordLimitViolation(GTNetMessageContext context)
      Records that the peer sent more than the entity's maxLimit allows.

      The counter saturates at 99 and is what isBlockedByRequestViolations(GTNetMessageContext) reads, so a peer that keeps overshooting eventually stops being served until an administrator resets it. Call it once per refused request, never per over-limit element.

      Parameters:
      context - the message context of the incoming request

    • hasExchangeGrant

      protected boolean hasExchangeGrant(GTNetMessageContext context, IExchangeKindType kind)
      Whether the peer holds an accepted, unrevoked grant for this exchange kind.

      Callers apply this directly after their own accept-flag check. The accept flag says whether this instance serves the kind at all; the grant says whether it serves it to this peer. Both are required, and a missing grant is answered with the code's own refusal where it has one, otherwise as a ProcessingError carrying GTNetGrantService.NO_GRANT, which reaches the peer as GT_NET_ERROR_S.

      Parameters:
      context - the message context of the incoming request
      kind - the exchange kind being asked for
      Returns:
      true when the peer may be served this kind

    • isBlockedByRequestViolations

      protected boolean isBlockedByRequestViolations(GTNetMessageContext context)
      Reports whether the remote server has run up so many request violations that its requests are no longer served. A violation is recorded by GTNetConfig.incrementRequestViolationCount() whenever the remote exceeds the max_limit configured for an exchange kind. The counter saturates at 99 and is compared against the global parameter g.max.limit.request.exceeded.count (default 20). Once the threshold is reached the remote stays refused until an administrator resets the counter through the GTNet configuration dialog, which is why GTNetConfig.requestViolationCount is updatable. Callers apply this guard directly after their own accept check and answer with the limit-exceeded code of their exchange kind, without incrementing the counter any further.
      Parameters:
      context - the message context of the incoming request
      Returns:
      true when the remote is over its violation budget and the request must not be served
